LESSON: WRITING 4.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue, part of Strand 4 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we write a good imaginative dialogue?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline the main features of a well-written dialogue,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compose an imaginative dialogue on the theme of environmental conservation for self- efficacy,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. promote creative writing for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. outline the main features of a well-written dialogue,

   Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. compose an imaginative dialogue on the theme of environmental conservation for self- efficacy,

   Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. promote creative writing for effective communication.

   Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search from electronic and library sources for imaginative dialogues,

2. watch or read the dialogues and discuss their features,

3. work with peers to develop an outline of the structure of a good dialogue on a chart,

4. write a simple imaginative dialogue on environmental conservation,

5. share the written dialogues with peers for review,

6. role play the dialogue with peers in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search from electronic and library sources for imaginative dialogues,
2. watch or read the dialogues and discuss their features,
3. work with peers to develop an outline of the structure of a good dialogue on a chart,
4. write a simple imaginative dialogue on environmental conservation,
5. share the written dialogues with peers for review,
6. role play the dialogue with peers in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.3.1 Creative Writing – Dialogue together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is nurtured as the learner contributes to group decision-making to develop an

outline of the structure of a good dialogue.

• Digital Literacy: This is acquired as the learner interacts with digital content to find sample imaginative dialogues.

Values:
• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner accommodates ideas from peers as they discuss features of a good dialogue.

• Responsibility: This is cultivated as the learner exhibits accountability to accept input when peer-reviewing

imaginative dialogues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peace education is enhanced as the learner embraces the role of dialogue for peaceful coexistence.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of dialogue writing to their learning in Kiswahili and English.

Main points to remember:

1. outline the main features of a well-written dialogue,
2. compose an imaginative dialogue on the theme of environmental conservation for self- efficacy,
3. promote creative writing for effective communication.

Remember the key question: How can we write a good imaginative dialogue?
